# Sources, provenance and search log

All page numbers refer to the printed pagination. "Read" means the text was read in this run
(text layer, or page images for the two scanned Kyushu memoirs); "checked" means the statement was
re-derived or recomputed here.

## Primary sources on the crystallographic groups

1. **J. Kaneko, S. Tokunaga, M. Yoshida, *Complex crystallographic groups II*, J. Math. Soc. Japan
   34 (1982) 595–605.** Local copy `complex-crystallographic-ii.pdf` (text layer present; read in full).
   * §1 (p. 595): definition of `G(m,p,2) ⊂ U(2)` as generated by `(0 1;1 0)`, `diag(θ⁻¹,θ)`,
     `diag(θᵖ,1)`, `θ = exp(2πi/m)`; definition of reflection.
   * **Theorem 1 (p. 596)**: every two-dimensional complex crystallographic group with `X/Γ ≅ P²` is
     affinely conjugate to one of the six groups `(2,1)₀ = G(2,1,2) ⋉ L²(τ)`, `(3,1)₀ = G(3,1,2) ⋉ L²(ζ)`,
     `(4,1)₀ = G(4,1,2) ⋉ L²(i)`, `(6,1)₀ = G(6,1,2) ⋉ L²(ζ)`,
     `(4,2)₁ = G(4,2,2) ⋉ {L²(i) + Z·((1+i)/2)(1,1)}`,
     `(3,3)₀ = G(3,3,2) ⋉ {L(τ)(−1,1) + L(τ)(ζ²,ζ)}`, with `L(τ) = Z + τZ`, `Im τ > 0`, `ζ = exp(2πi/6)`.
     Checked: the list is exactly the six rows of Table II of Part I (below) whose quotient type is `(1,1,1)`.
   * Theorem 2 (pp. 596–597): generators and relations (used only for the point-group orders).
   * **Theorem 3 (pp. 599–600)**: coordinate representation of `φ: X → M` and branch data. Rows
     `(m,1)₀`: `φ(x,y) = (P(x)+P(y) : P(x)P(y) : 1)` with `P = ℘`, `℘′`, `℘²`, `℘′²` for `m = 2,3,4,6`,
     i.e. the quotient factors through `E×E → (E/C_m)×(E/C_m) = P¹×P¹ → Sym²P¹ = P²`; branch divisor
     "4 lines and a conic tangent to each line" for `(2,1)₀`, "3 lines and a conic" for `(3,1)₀`.
     Row `(4,2)₁`: `φ = ( ((℘℘+e₁²)/(℘℘−e₁²))² : ((℘+℘)/(℘℘−e₁²))² : 1 )`, `e₁ = ℘(1/2 | i)`; branch divisor
     six lines. Row `(3,3)₀`: `φ(x₁,y₁) = (℘′(x₁)−℘′(y₁) : ℘(x₁)−℘(y₁) : ℘′(x₁)℘(y₁)−℘(x₁)℘′(y₁))`, branch
     divisor the dual curve of the nonsingular cubic of modulus `τ`, ramification index 2.
   * Remark 1 (p. 600): `Σ d_j (1 − 1/e_j) = 3` for every row (checked for the `(m,1)₀` rows).
   * Proof of Theorem 3 (pp. 601–602): `(2,1)₀ ◁ (4,2)₁` (modulus `τ = i`) with quotient group
     `{diag(±1,±1,1)}` acting on the `(2,1)₀`-quotient plane; for `(3,3)₀`, in the coordinates
     `(x₁,y₁)` the group is `⟨(−1 −1; 0 1), (0 1; 1 0)⟩ ⋉ L²(τ)` and `X/Γ₀ ≅ E×E → P²` is given by
     Abel's theorem (lines through pairs of points of the plane cubic `η(E)`).
2. **S. Tokunaga, M. Yoshida, *Complex crystallographic groups I*, J. Math. Soc. Japan 34 (1982)
   581–593.** Local copy `complex-crystallographic-i.pdf` (text layer; §5 read).
   * **Theorem 5.1 and Table II (pp. 589–590)**: the twenty two-dimensional crystallographic reflection
     groups with their lattices and the weighted-projective type of the quotient. Rows of type `(1,1,1)`:
     `(2,1)₀`, `(4,2)₁`, `(4,1)₀`, `(3,1)₀`, `(6,1)₀`, `(3,3)₀` — exactly the six groups of Part II,
     Theorem 1.
   * Proposition 5.2 (p. 591): index-two inclusions, in particular `(2,1)₀ ◁ (4,2)₀ ◁ (4,1)₀`,
     `(4,2)₁ ∼◁ (4,2)₀`, `(3,1)₀ ◁ (6,2)₀ ◁ (6,1)₀`, `(3,3)₀ ◁ (6,6)₀`. Used for the observation that
     `(4,2)₁` is conjugate to an index-four subgroup of `(4,1)₀` (checked directly: the similarity
     `s = (1+i)/2` gives `s(4,1)₀s⁻¹ ⊃ (4,2)₁`).

## Primary sources on the Kühnel triangulation and its crystallographic construction

3. **B. Morin, M. Yoshida, *The Kühnel triangulation of the complex projective plane from the view
   point of complex crystallography, Part I*, Mem. Fac. Sci. Kyushu Univ. Ser. A 45 (1991) 55–142.**
   Downloaded from https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/kyushumfs/45/1/45_1_55/_pdf (scan, no text
   layer); pages read as images: 55–64, 84, 89–116, 129.
   * §1 (pp. 58–60): `K` is the union of the `G`-orbits of `(1 2 4 5 9)` (27 simplices) and
     `(1 2 4 5 6)` (9 simplices), `G = ⟨α,β,γ⟩` of order 27 acting on the array `((1,4,7),(2,5,8),(3,6,9))`.
     **Checked**: regenerating `K` from this description gives exactly the 36 facets of Kühnel–Banchoff.
   * §2 (pp. 61–64): the link `ℳ` of vertex 9 is the sphere denoted `ℳ` in Grünbaum–Sreedharan, one of
     the four neighbourly 8-vertex 3-spheres (8, 28, 40, 20), non-polytopal; `|K|` is PL.
   * §5 (p. 84): `T ∩ ℳ` is the trefoil `14∪43∪35∪52∪26∪61`; `T` models the dual of a nonsingular cubic
     (9 cusps); announcement of `K̃`, `Γ`, `Γ″` and the map `Y: C² → CP²` with `|K| = |K̃/Γ|`.
   * §6 (pp. 93–101): the sixfold cover `ℳ̃` of `ℳ` branched along the trefoil (30 vertices, 120
     tetrahedra), realised in `C²` as `∂𝒩`.
   * **§7 (pp. 105–108)**: `L(ω) = Z + Zω`; vectors `e_i, f_j, h_j`; lattices `L[h] ⊂₉ L[f] ⊂₃ L[e]`;
     `σ = diag(ω,ω²)`, `τ = (0 −1; −1 0)`, `γ̃ = ω²·I`; `G₆ = ⟨σ,τ⟩`, `G₁₈ = ⟨G₆, γ̃⟩`;
     **`Γ = L[h] ⋊ G₆`, `Γ″ = L[f] ⋊ G₁₈`**; reflection lines `L[f] + Cf_j`, meeting in threes at `L[f]`;
     colours `L₁,…,L₉ = L[f]/L[h]`; `Γ″/Γ ≅ G`.
   * §8 (pp. 109–116): the hyperplane arrangement `Σ = Γ″Π`, `Π = {Re(z₁+z₂)=0}`; Claim 1 (p. 111)
     the cells of `C² − |Σ|` are 4-simplices or 3–3 cells; the 3–3 cells are split in a `Γ″`-invariant
     way (two choices, exchanged by `ε̃`; the one matching Kühnel–Banchoff is taken); all 4-simplices
     have volume 3/32; **Claim 2 (p. 116): `K̃/Γ ≅ K` as abstract complexes.**
   * Footnote p. 106: the hexagonal symmetry is not needed; with `Z + Zτ` one still gets a
     triangulation combinatorially equal to `K̃` (§12 of Part II).
   * **Checked here** (`scripts/verify_33_identification.py`, exact arithmetic in `Q(ω)`):
     `|G₆| = 6`, `D·G(3,3,2)·D⁻¹ = G₆` for `D = diag(1,−1)`, and `(ω²−ω)⁻¹·D⁻¹L[h] = L(ω)(−1,1) + L(ω)(ζ²,ζ)`.
     Hence Morin–Yoshida's `Γ` is affinely conjugate to the row `(3,3)₀` at `τ = ω`.
4. **P. Arnoux, A. Marin, same title, Part II, Mem. Fac. Sci. Kyushu Univ. Ser. A 45 (1991) 167–244.**
   Downloaded from https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/kyushumfs/45/2/45_2_167/_pdf (scan); pages
   read: 167–185, 203–204.
   * §12 (pp. 171–172): the Yoshida crystal `CPⁿ = A/S_{n+1}`, `A = {Σz_i = 0} ⊂ E^{n+1}`; the
     `S_{n+1}`-fixed points are the `(n+1)²` points `(z,…,z)`, `z ∈ E[n+1]`; splitting `A = T′×T`.
   * §13 (pp. 172–175): the real crystal `T/S_{n+1}` (affine Weyl group of type `A_n`), fundamental
     simplex `Δ`, Dirichlet domain `ℋ`.
   * **§14 (pp. 176–179)**: the *weak prismatic decomposition* of `T′×T/S_{n+1}` into `(n+1)!` flat prisms
     `Δ′×Δ·σ` all sharing the same `(n+1)²` vertices; definition of *(admissible) diagonalisation*
     (linear subdivision into simplices adding no vertex, compatible on common subprisms, every simplex
     determined by its vertex set); **Proposition 1: for `n ≥ 3` no admissible diagonalisation exists**;
     **Proposition 2 (p. 179): for `n ≤ 2` an admissible diagonalisation exists and is unique modulo
     the quarter turn `C₄`; for `n = 2` the four diagonalisations are all isomorphic to Kühnel's complex.**
   * §15 (pp. 179–185): the proof (tables `t_k`, Claims 1–4, Figure 13.5 "Kühnel's diagonalisation").
   * §20 (pp. 203–204): Kühnel complexes of weight `w` and height `n`; Conjectures 0–2.
5. **W. Kühnel, T. F. Banchoff, *The 9-vertex complex projective plane*, Math. Intelligencer 5 (1983)
   no. 3, 11–22.** Local copy (text layer). Table of 36 facets on pp. 14–15 (transcribed to
   `data/cp2_9_facets_kuhnel_banchoff_1983.txt`); symmetry group of order 54, `G₂₇`, isotropy of a vertex
   of order 6 (p. 15); the link is "denoted `ℳ` in [Grünbaum–Sreedharan]", non-polytopal, any two
   tetrahedra meet (p. 14). **Checked**: identical as a set to the Chapoton–Manivel transcription
   already stored in `runs/cp2-nine-vertex-equivariant-t2-2026-09-09/data/`.
6. **B. Bagchi, B. Datta, *On Kühnel's 9-vertex complex projective plane*, Geom. Dedicata 50 (1994)
   1–13.** Local copy (text layer; pp. 1–3 read). Uniqueness of `CP²₉`; the link of a vertex is the
   Brückner–Grünbaum sphere, "the only neighbourly 8-vertex `S³` in which any two tetrahedra intersect"
   (p. 2); full automorphism group of order 54 (p. 3).
7. **W. Kühnel, G. Lassmann, *The unique 3-neighborly 4-manifold with few vertices*, J. Combin.
   Theory Ser. A 35 (1983) 173–184.** Local copy; not needed beyond the uniqueness statement.

## Bagchi–Datta ten-vertex triangulation

8. **B. Bagchi, B. Datta, *From the icosahedron to natural triangulations of `CP²` and `S²×S²`*,
   arXiv:1004.3157 (2010).** TeX source downloaded (`bd11.tex`) and read (Sections 1, 4, 5).
   * Section 1: `(S²×S²)₁₆` = the unique (up to isomorphism) `Z₂`-symmetric *pure* simplicial subdivision
     of the cell complex `S²₄ × S²₄` without new vertices (**Theorem 1**: exactly two such complexes, they
     are isomorphic); vertices `x_ij`, automorphism group `A₄ × Z₂`, five basic facets, f-vector
     `(16,84,216,240,96)`. `CP²₁₀ := (S²×S²)₁₆/Z₂`, vertices `x_ij (i ≤ j)`, basic facets
     `x₁₁x₂₂x₃₃x₁₂x₁₃, x₁₁x₂₂x₁₂x₁₄x₃₄, x₁₁x₂₂x₁₄x₂₄x₃₄, x₁₁x₂₂x₁₂x₁₃x₂₄, x₁₁x₂₂x₁₃x₂₄x₃₄` modulo
     `A₄ = ⟨(123),(12)(34)⟩`; f-vector `(10,45,110,120,48)`; 2-neighbourly; automorphism group `A₄`.
   * Section 4: the self-dual CW decomposition of `CP²` with f-vector `(10,24,31,24,10)`.
   * Section 5 (Definition "pure", Lemma 1): a pure action gives a simplicial quotient triangulating
     the orbit space; `CP²₁₀` triangulates `CP²` and induces the standard PL structure.
   * **Checked**: both complexes regenerated from the basic facets and groups; f-vectors, automorphism
     group orders (24 and 12), the product-cell structure (16 cells, 6 simplices each, each a genuine
     geometric triangulation of `Δ₂×Δ₂`), purity of the swap, `CP²₁₀ = (S²×S²)₁₆/swap`.

## Deformation theory of Stanley–Reisner schemes

9. **K. Altmann, J. A. Christophersen, *Deforming Stanley–Reisner schemes*, Math. Ann. 348 (2010)
   513–537; arXiv:0901.2502.** PDF downloaded and read (Sections 1, 2, 4, 5).
   * Theorem 4.1 ([AC04, Thm 13]) and Proposition 4.2: `T^i_{a−b}` of `A_K` via `lk(a)`; Definition 4.4
     of `B(K)`; Theorem 4.6: `dim T¹_{A_K,c} = 1 iff a ∈ K and b ∈ B(lk(a,K))`; Table 1 (p. 10).
   * Proposition 4.8: `T²_{∅−b}` for manifolds; Theorem 5.5: `H⁰(T¹_{P(K)}) ≅ T¹_{A_K,0}`,
     `0 → H¹(Θ) → T¹_{P(K)} → H⁰(T¹_{P(K)}) → 0`; Theorem 5.7 (3-manifolds):
     `dim T¹_{P(K)} = 11d₃ + 5e₃ + 3e₄ + e_{≥5} + c_{≥6} + 5f₁⁽³⁾ + 2f₁⁽⁴⁾ + h²(K)`; Corollary 5.8: `P(K)` is
     rigid if `H²(K) = 0` and all edges have valency ≥ 5; Example 5.10: `dim T²_{∂C(8,4),0} = 64`.
   * The paper contains **no smoothing theorem for triangulated 3-spheres**; smoothings of spheres are
     mentioned as the motivation ("if possible, Calabi–Yau", p. 1).
   * **Checked**: `scripts/t1_formula.py` implements Definition 4.4 and Theorem 4.6 and reproduces the
     Macaulay2 values 53, 54, 63 for the three links; Theorem 5.7 gives the same numbers.
10. **I. Fausk, *Pfaffian Calabi–Yau threefolds, Stanley–Reisner schemes and mirror symmetry*, PhD
    thesis, University of Oslo 2012; arXiv:1205.4871.** Local TeX source `fausk.tex` (read: Chapter 3).
    Table 3.1 (Grünbaum–Sreedharan's five 3-spheres `P⁷₁,…,P⁷₅` with 7 vertices) and the summary theorem
    (Table 3.2): `P⁷₁` (degree 11) non-smoothable, general fibre with one node, small resolution has
    `h¹²=86`; `P⁷₂, P⁷₃` (degree 12) smooth to complete intersections of type `(2,2,3)` with
    `h¹¹=1, h¹²=73`, versal base of dimension 79; `P⁷₄` (degree 13) to the Pfaffian CY3 of a `5×5` matrix
    with quadratic first row, `h¹¹=1, h¹²=61`, dimension 67; `P⁷₅` (degree 14) to the Pfaffian CY3 of a
    general `7×7` linear matrix, `h¹¹=1, h¹²=50`, dimension 56. These are the only published smoothing
    theorems for SR schemes of 3-spheres that we found; none concerns a 9-vertex sphere.
11. **The sphere problem of this repository** (`PROOFS.md`, `reports/GEOGRAPHY.md`, `runs/astra-*`,
    source packet `grunbaum-zero-context-proof` at `ee984e9541e9cb9259728e6dc7b3a1bc0fda8a9b`): degree 20,
    Hilbert polynomial `(10/3)m³ + (14/3)m`, `c₂·H = 56` under the smooth-fibre hypothesis (GEO-003),
    `(h¹¹,h²¹) = (1,31)`, `ρ = 1`, `χ = −60` **PROVED within the accepted zero-context smoothing trust
    boundary** (C05), not independently refereed. Used only as the status record for the `(3,3)₀` row.

## Other sources consulted

12. **J. Sawon, *Isotrivial elliptic K3 surfaces and Lagrangian fibrations*, arXiv:1406.1233**, TeX
    source read (§2.2, §3.1–3.2): the Kummer-type K3 surfaces `E×E/C_m` (`m = 2,3,4,6`) with their
    isotrivial elliptic fibrations, `Hilbⁿ S → Sym^n P¹ = Pⁿ`, `K_n(A) → Pⁿ`, and the Question whether
    `Pⁿ` arises as `B/Γ` in other ways. These describe fourfolds over the same bases `E²/(C_m ≀ S₂)` and
    `E²/S₃` but say nothing about SR schemes of links; recorded as context only.
13. **B. Grünbaum, V. P. Sreedharan, *An enumeration of simplicial 4-polytopes with 8 vertices*,
    J. Combin. Theory 2 (1967) 437–465** (local copy) and **D. Barnette, *The triangulations of the
    3-sphere with up to 8 vertices*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 14 (1973) 37–52** (local copy): the
    catalogue background for "Brückner–Grünbaum sphere `ℳ`". Not re-read in detail; the identification
    of the link with the packet's sphere was done by an exact isomorphism instead.
14. **D. Panov, *Polyhedral Kähler manifolds*, Geom. Topol. 13 (2009)**, and the notes
    `avatars.pdf` (local): searched for "Kühnel"/"crystallographic"; no statements about the links.
15. `heap-project/stanley-reisner.tex` (the user's notes): mentions Kühnel–Banchoff and guesses that
    `ℳ` is the vertex figure of `CP²₉` — confirmed here by exact isomorphism. `sr-project`,
    `grunbaum-cy-geography-fable-dgla`: no material on `CP²₁₀`, the crystallographic rows or their links.

## Search log for unresolved items

* Smoothing of SR schemes of **9-vertex 3-spheres** to CY3s in `P⁸`: web searches
  ("Stanley-Reisner" 3-sphere "9 vertices" Calabi–Yau `P^8`; "neighborly" 3-sphere 9 vertices
  Stanley–Reisner Calabi–Yau degree 27; Calabi–Yau threefold `P^8` degree 27 or 22 codimension 5) returned
  only Fausk (7 vertices), Altmann–Christophersen (general theory), arXiv:2011.10871 (CY3s in `Pⁿ` and
  Gorenstein rings; the codimension-five examples there are not SR degenerations of these links) and
  Coughlan–Gołębiowski–Kapustka–Kapustka (`P⁷`). **Nothing found** for the two `CP²₁₀` links; status
  "not found" in the table. The arithmetically Gorenstein codimension-5 setting has no structure theorem,
  so no general existence result applies.
* A published `(4,2)₁`-compatible triangulation of `CP²`: **not found**; the only published
  crystallographic triangulation is Kühnel's (row `(3,3)₀`).
* A published statement that `CP²₁₀` is the `(2,1)₀` (or any `(m,1)₀`) quotient triangulation: **not
  found**; Bagchi–Datta work with `S²₄×S²₄` combinatorially and never mention lattices. The compatibility
  is established here computationally (`scripts/lifts.py`).
